lessons.title: Who refers, and why it matters
lessons.intro: Every inpatient or outpatient case starts with someone sending the patient. For the hospital, referring doctors behave like B2B customers: they decide where patients go.

followUp.q: Name two identifiers a Swiss referring doctor has, and what each is used for.
followUp.a: GLN (Global Location Number, unique ID of the person/organisation in Swiss health registries) and ZSR number (SASIS creditor number, used for billing to insurers). Both should be correct in the referrer's master data.

sections.title: What happens and who is involved
paragraphs: A referral (Zuweisung, Überweisung) is a request from one provider to another: please examine, treat or admit this patient. It usually contains the question (Fragestellung), urgency, relevant diagnoses and medication, insurance details and the referring doctor's contact data.

actors.role: GP (Hausärztin), specialist, other hospital. Writes the referral, expects a report back.
Receives the referral, checks completeness, books or forwards it.
Decides urgency and the right clinic or service.
Brings insurance card, may choose the hospital within the rules of the insurance model.
In managed-care models (HMO, Hausarztmodell), a missing referral can mean the insurer refuses or reduces payment.

sections.title: SAP IS-H: where it lands
bullets: External doctors are stored as IS-H business partners (table NGPA), with identifiers such as GLN and ZSR.
GLN (Global Location Number): unique 13-digit ID of a health professional or organisation in Swiss registries. ZSR number: creditor number issued by SASIS, used when billing insurers.
The referring physician is linked to the case (NFAL) as referring / admitting doctor.
The referral letter itself usually lives in the clinical system (for you today: KISIM) or a referral portal, not in IS-H.
If the business partner is duplicated or outdated, every downstream document (report, invoice) inherits the error.

sections.title: Epic: the same step
bullets: Referrals: a referral record with status, priority, referring and referred-to provider, linked to visits.
EpicCare Link: web portal where external referrers can send referrals and see results.
Work queues route incomplete or new referrals to the right team.

sections.title: Interfaces and standards
bullets: Today often: letter, fax or secure HIN mail, then manual entry.
Structured: referral portals and eHealth Suisse exchange formats (e.g. CH ORF, FHIR-based order & referral forms).
HL7 v2 has referral messages (REF), but in Swiss practice portals and FHIR are more relevant.

verify.note: Check the current status and adoption of CH ORF and other exchange formats.

sections.title: Tariffs and regulation
bullets: The referral itself is rarely a billable service, but the referring doctor appears on the invoice.
Alternative insurance models (HMO, Hausarztmodell, Telmed) under KVG: patients agree to see a gatekeeper first. Without a referral the insurer may refuse to pay.

verify.note: Rules of alternative insurance models are set per insurer and product. Verify current practice with the insurers your hospital works with.

sections.title: Business analyst view
bullets: Typical problems: incomplete referrals, unclear urgency, duplicate referrer records, no feedback loop to the referrer.
Improvement ideas: structured e-referral with mandatory fields, master data stewardship for referrers, referrer dashboard (volumes, waiting times).

kpis.name: Referral-to-first-contact time
kpis.formula: Days between referral received and first appointment

kpis.name: Complete referral rate
kpis.formula: Referrals with all mandatory fields ÷ all referrals

kpis.name: Referrer concentration
kpis.formula: Share of cases from top 20 referrers

market.title: Swiss market: referrers decide volume
market.body: With more outpatient care and fixed tariffs, hospitals compete for referrers. Many build Zuweiser portals and referrer relationship teams. A BA who understands both the data and the relationship side is valuable here.

scenario.title: Rejected for a missing referral
scenario.situation: An insurer rejects an outpatient invoice: the patient has an HMO model and the invoice shows no referring doctor. The secretariat says the GP did send a letter by HIN mail.
scenario.question: Where is the root cause, and what would you fix at the source?
steps: Root cause: the referral existed, but the referring doctor was never linked to the case, so it was missing on the invoice.
Short term: link the referring doctor (correct business partner with GLN/ZSR) and resend the invoice.
At the source: make the referrer a mandatory field when a case is created for patients in managed-care models.
Measure: rejections with reason 'missing referral' per month, target close to zero.

quiz.q: Where is the referral letter itself usually stored in a hospital with IS-H and KISIM?
o: In the clinical system or a referral portal
quiz.x: IS-H stores the referring doctor and the case; the letter is a clinical document.

quiz.q: Which IS-H object holds external doctors such as GPs?
quiz.x: External physicians are business partners with identifiers such as GLN and ZSR.

quiz.q: Why can a missing referral lead to an invoice rejection?
o: In managed-care models the insurer requires a gatekeeper referral
The canton pays only with a referral
quiz.x: HMO and Hausarzt models require the patient to go through the gatekeeper first.

exercise.title: Telefonnotiz aus dem Sekretariat
exercise.instruction: Choose the right word for each gap. This is a typical phone note in a clinic.
exercise.text: Frau Dr. Keller hat eine {0} für Herrn Bühler geschickt. Die {1} ist: Knieschmerzen seit drei Monaten. Die {2} ist mittel, er {3} in den nächsten zwei Wochen einen Termin bekommen.
exercise.translation: Dr Keller sent a referral for Mr Bühler. The question is: knee pain for three months. Urgency is medium; he should get an appointment within the next two weeks.

lessons.title: From letter to data: front end vs. back end
lessons.intro: This lesson connects what you click in SAP GUI with what is stored underneath. It is the foundation of the architecture map in this app.

followUp.q: In SAP GUI, how do you find out which table and field sit behind a screen field?
followUp.a: Click into the field, press F1, then 'Technical information'. It shows the screen field, table or structure and field name. If it shows a structure, the data is usually stored in a table with a similar name.

sections.title: What happens
paragraphs: The secretariat reads the referral and turns it into structured data: find or create the patient, link the referring doctor, create a planned case or appointment request. Each click writes into specific database tables.

sections.title: Three layers in SAP IS-H

items.label: Front end (SAP GUI)
items.detail: Transactions such as NP01–NP03 (patient), NV2000 (case and patient processing). You see tabs, fields, a 'Bemerkung' (remark) text.

items.label: Application (ABAP logic)
items.detail: Checks and rules: mandatory fields, duplicate check, insurance validations, status. Customizing controls much of this.

items.label: Database (tables)
items.detail: NPAT patient, NFAL case, NBEW movements, NLEI services, NGPA business partners, NORG organisational units. Long texts like remarks are often stored separately as SAP texts linked to the object.

bullets: Your daily work in cost approval: you document the insurer's answer in a remark. Whether that remark belongs to the patient, the case or the insurance relationship matters: a patient-level note is visible on every future case, a case-level note only on this stay.
Exercise for your next shift: click into the 'Bemerkung' field you use, press F1 → Technical information, and write down the structure/table and field name. Bring it to the Architecture map.

sections.title: Epic comparison
bullets: Epic stores data in its own database (Chronicles) with master files (e.g. patient, encounter/HAR, coverage, referral).
Same principle: front-end activities (Prelude registration) write to records; Clarity/Caboodle copy the data to a reporting database.

sections.title: Why the back end matters for interfaces
bullets: Interfaces send records, not screens: an HL7 ADT message carries patient (PID) and visit (PV1) data from tables, not your remark text.
A note in a free-text field is invisible to most interfaces, reports and automations. Structured fields travel; free text stays.

sections.title: Business analyst view
bullets: Free text is the enemy of automation and reporting. If people document cost approval only as a remark, no KPI and no bot can read it reliably.
Improvement idea: move key facts (approved yes/no, approved until, insurer reference) into structured fields, keep the remark for exceptions.

kpis.name: Structured documentation rate
kpis.formula: Cases with structured cost-approval status ÷ cases requiring approval

market.title: Why this skill transfers to Epic
market.body: Every migration (IS-H → Epic) is a data mapping exercise: which IS-H field goes to which Epic item. People who understand front end, logic and tables are needed in data migration and validation teams.

scenario.title: The invisible remark
scenario.situation: Controlling wants a weekly list of inpatient cases where cost approval is still open. Today this information exists only in remarks.
scenario.question: What do you propose?
steps: Confirm where the remark is stored (F1 → Technical information).
Short term: a text search report is fragile; agree on a fixed keyword format only as a bridge.
Target: a structured status field (e.g. cost coverage status on the insurance relationship) maintained in the process.
Write user stories and test cases; train the team; measure the share of cases with structured status.

quiz.q: Which IS-H table holds the case?
quiz.x: NFAL = case. NPAT = patient, NORG = organisational unit, NGPA = business partner.

quiz.q: What does F1 → Technical information show you?
o: The table/structure and field behind a screen field
quiz.x: This is your fastest bridge from front end to back end.

quiz.q: Why is free text a problem for interfaces and reports?
o: It cannot be read reliably by systems
quiz.x: Structured fields are machine-readable; remarks are not.

exercise.title: Anleitung für eine neue Kollegin
exercise.instruction: Fill in the gaps with the correct form.
exercise.text: Zuerst {0} du den Patienten im System. Dann {1} du die Daten der Zuweisung. Das Geburtsdatum ist ein {2}. Wichtige Informationen schreibst du nicht nur in die {3}.
exercise.translation: First you search for the patient in the system. Then you enter the referral data. Date of birth is a mandatory field. You don't write important information only in the remark.

lessons.title: Triage and your first BPMN model
lessons.intro: Not every referral is equally urgent. Triage decides who is seen when. Today you also model the referral intake as a BPMN process.

followUp.q: Name the four BPMN elements you used yesterday.
followUp.a: Pool/lanes (who), start and end events, tasks (activities), and gateways (decisions, e.g. 'referral complete?').

sections.title: What happens
paragraphs: For planned care, a doctor (or a trained nurse with rules) reviews the referral and assigns a priority, e.g. within 48 hours, 2 weeks or 3 months. Emergency departments use structured triage scales such as the Emergency Severity Index (ESI) or Manchester Triage.

actors.role: Clinical decision on urgency and service.
Checks completeness first, then books according to priority.
Gets a confirmation or a request for missing information.

sections.title: SAP IS-H
bullets: Urgency and triage are typically documented in the clinical system, not in IS-H core.
IS-H receives the outcome: planned admission date, organisational unit (NORG), case type.

sections.title: Epic
bullets: Referral priority and status in the referral record; Cadence work queues sort by priority; ED triage in ASAP (emergency module).

sections.title: BA track: BPMN basics

items.label: Pool and lanes
items.detail: Who does the work: Referrer, Secretariat, Triage doctor.

items.label: Events
items.detail: Start: 'Referral received'. End: 'Appointment booked' or 'Referral returned'.

items.label: Tasks
items.detail: Check completeness, Triage, Book appointment, Confirm to referrer.

items.label: Gateways
items.detail: Diamond with a question: 'Complete?' yes/no, 'Urgent?' yes/no.

bullets: As-is first, to-be later. Model what really happens, including workarounds, not what the manual says.

kpis.name: Time to triage
kpis.formula: Hours between referral received and triage decision

kpis.name: Return rate
kpis.formula: Referrals sent back for missing info ÷ all referrals

market.title: BPMN in Swiss hospitals
market.body: Process models are standard in Epic and IS-H projects: as-is workshops with clinics, then to-be models that become requirements. Tools vary (Signavio, ADONIS, Visio, draw.io); the notation is the same.

scenario.title: Model the intake
scenario.situation: Draw on paper the as-is process: a referral arrives by HIN mail at the orthopaedics secretariat. If information is missing, the secretariat calls the GP. Then a doctor triages, and the secretariat books an appointment.
scenario.question: Which lanes, tasks and gateways does your model need?
steps: Task: Check completeness → Gateway 'Complete?' → No: Task 'Request missing info' (message to GP) and wait; Yes: continue.
Task: Triage (doctor) → Gateway 'Urgency?' → book within 48 h / 2 weeks / 3 months.
Task: Book appointment → Task: Confirm to patient and referrer → End event.

quiz.q: Which BPMN element represents a decision?
quiz.x: Gateways (diamonds) split or merge the flow.

quiz.q: What should an as-is model show?
quiz.x: The to-be model comes after you understand reality.

quiz.q: Where is triage usually documented in a hospital with IS-H and a clinical system?
quiz.x: IS-H receives the outcome (planned date, unit).

exercise.title: Rückfrage an die Hausarztpraxis
exercise.instruction: Write 2–3 sentences in German: ask the GP practice for the missing medication list. Use 'weil' or 'dass' once.
hints: Guten Tag, hier ist das Sekretariat der Orthopädie.
Die Zuweisung ist leider unvollständig, weil …
exercise.model: Guten Tag, hier ist das Sekretariat der Orthopädie. Die Zuweisung für Herrn Bühler ist leider unvollständig, weil die Medikamentenliste fehlt. Könnten Sie uns die Liste bitte per HIN-Mail schicken?

lessons.title: Interoperability: HL7, FHIR, EPD and the Epic shift
lessons.intro: Referral data travels between systems. Today: which standards matter in Switzerland, and how the move to Epic changes the landscape.

followUp.q: What is the difference between HL7 v2 and FHIR in one sentence each?
followUp.a: HL7 v2: pipe-delimited messages pushed between systems (e.g. ADT A01), widely used inside hospitals. FHIR: modern standard with resources (Patient, Encounter, ServiceRequest) exchanged via web APIs, used more and more for cross-organisation exchange.

items.label: HL7 v2
items.detail: Messages between hospital systems: ADT (patient movements), ORM/ORU (orders/results), SIU (appointments). IS-H sends and receives them via its communication module (HCM) or an integration engine.

items.label: FHIR
items.detail: Resources like Patient, Practitioner, ServiceRequest, Appointment. Used by eHealth Suisse exchange formats and modern APIs.

items.label: EPD
items.detail: Electronic patient record (elektronisches Patientendossier): patients can store documents such as discharge letters. The legal basis is being revised.

items.label: HIN
items.detail: Secure email and identity network widely used by Swiss doctors.

verify.note: EPD legislation (EPDG revision) and adoption change over time. Check the current state before quoting it in an interview.

sections.title: SAP IS-H lifecycle
bullets: SAP has announced the end of maintenance for IS-H. Mainstream maintenance runs to end of 2027, extended maintenance to 2030.
This is why many Swiss hospitals are selecting new systems now. IS-H know-how stays valuable during migration and parallel operation.

verify.note: Confirm the exact maintenance dates in SAP's official announcements.

sections.title: Epic in Switzerland
bullets: Luzerner Kantonsspital was an early Swiss Epic customer (go-live 2019); Insel Gruppe Bern followed (go-live 2024). More hospitals are in selection or implementation.
Epic integrates clinical and administrative modules in one database, so the KISIM ↔ IS-H interface world gets simpler, but insurer and canton interfaces stay.

verify.note: Check current Swiss Epic customers and go-live dates in recent press releases.

sections.title: Business analyst view
bullets: In a migration, every interface is a requirement: which messages, which fields, which errors, who monitors.
Good interface requirements name: trigger, sender, receiver, data elements, error handling, monitoring owner.

kpis.name: Interface error rate
kpis.formula: Failed messages ÷ all messages per day

kpis.name: Time to fix
kpis.formula: Hours until a failed message is reprocessed

market.title: What the shift means for you
market.body: Short term: IS-H skills for operations and migration. Medium term: Epic analyst roles (certification is sponsored by the employer) and BA/PO roles that bridge clinics, finance and IT. Your edge: process and business understanding plus German.

scenario.title: Interface requirement
scenario.situation: In the future Epic landscape, referrals from a regional GP portal should arrive as structured data.
scenario.question: List the six elements of a good interface requirement for this.
steps: Trigger: GP submits a referral in the portal.
Sender / receiver: GP portal → Epic Referrals.
Format: FHIR ServiceRequest (or agreed national format).
Data elements: patient identity, insurance, referrer GLN, question, urgency, attachments.
Error handling: unmatched patient → work queue; missing mandatory data → reject with message to portal.
Monitoring owner: application team, daily error check, KPI error rate.

quiz.q: Which HL7 v2 message type reports patient movements like admission?
What is FHIR's basic building block?
quiz.x: FHIR uses resources such as Patient or Appointment.

quiz.q: Until when does SAP plan extended maintenance for IS-H (verify!)?
quiz.x: Mainstream to end of 2027, extended to 2030 according to SAP's announcement. Always verify the current state.

exercise.title: Info-Mail zur Systemumstellung
exercise.text: Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, im nächsten Jahr {0} ein neues Klinikinformationssystem eingeführt. Zuweisungen {1} dann elektronisch übermittelt. Alle Mitarbeitenden {2} vorher geschult.
exercise.translation: Dear colleagues, next year a new clinical information system will be introduced. Referrals will then be transmitted electronically. All staff will be trained beforehand.

lessons.title: BA exercise: user stories for complete referrals
lessons.intro: Stage finale. You turn the referral problems into user stories with acceptance criteria, the way a product owner would bring them to a backlog refinement.

followUp.a: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable – a checklist for good user stories.

sections.title: Requirements engineering basics

items.label: User story
items.detail: As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

items.label: Acceptance criteria
items.detail: Given <context>, when <action>, then <result>. Testable and specific.

items.label: INVEST
items.detail: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

items.label: Definition of Ready
items.detail: Story is clear, has acceptance criteria, dependencies known – ready for the sprint.

bullets: IREB CPRE calls this elicitation (find requirements), documentation (write them) and validation (check them with stakeholders).
Stories describe the need, not the solution. 'Mandatory field' is a solution; 'I can't save without the referrer' is the need.

baExercise.task: Write 3 user stories (with acceptance criteria) that reduce incomplete referrals and 'missing referral' rejections.
guidance: Pick three different roles: secretariat, referring GP, billing.
Each story: one sentence plus 2 acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then.
baExercise.template:
As a …, I want … so that …
Given …, when …, then …
Given …, when …, then …
model:
As a clinic secretary, I want the system to show which referral data is missing when I create a case so that I can request it on the same day.
Given a referral without referrer GLN, when I save the case, then a warning lists the missing field.
Given all mandatory referral data is present, when I save, then no warning appears.

As a referring GP, I want to submit referrals through a structured online form so that the hospital has everything it needs at once.
Given I leave 'question' empty, when I submit, then the form shows an error.
Given I submit a complete form, when it is received, then I get a confirmation with a reference number.

As a billing specialist, I want cases of patients in managed-care models to be blocked for invoicing until a referrer is linked so that we avoid rejections.
Given an HMO patient case without referrer, when invoicing runs, then the case appears on a work list with reason 'referrer missing'.
Given the referrer is linked, when invoicing runs again, then the invoice is created.
checklist: Role, need and benefit are clear
Each story is small enough for one sprint
No technical solution forced in the story sentence

quiz.q: Which part of a user story says WHY?
Which format is typical for acceptance criteria?
Which certification focuses on requirements engineering?
quiz.x: IREB Certified Professional for Requirements Engineering. IIBA (ECBA/CCBA/CBAP) is the business analysis alternative.

exercise.title: Eine User Story auf Deutsch
exercise.instruction: Translate one of your user stories into German. Use the pattern below.
exercise.model: Als Sekretärin möchte ich sehen, welche Angaben in der Zuweisung fehlen, damit ich sie am selben Tag nachfragen kann. Wenn die GLN der Zuweiserin fehlt, dann zeigt das System beim Speichern eine Warnung.
checklist: 'damit' clause with verb at the end
